intro: I build machine learning and deep learning models on biological and clinical data, and the reproducible Python pipelines that feed them.

My work spans PyTorch models trained on high-dimensional physiological signals, end-to-end single-cell and bulk transcriptomics workflows, and differential expression analysis of cancer genomics datasets. Six publications have come out of it — five IEEE conference papers across oncology, neurology, hematology and endocrinology, and a journal review on bioinformatics approaches to norovirus surveillance.
I am currently a Data Analyst on the core R&D team at Elmentoz Research Pvt. Ltd. while completing my final year of B.Tech Bioinformatics at Marwadi University.

about.label: About
about.heading: Computation first, biology always.
paragraphs: I am in the final year of a B.Tech in Bioinformatics at Marwadi University (NAAC A+). Since August 2026 I have also worked as a Data Analyst on the core R&D team at Elmentoz Research in Hyderabad, building and testing genomics pipelines.

The through-line in my work is applying predictive modelling to data that was generated to answer a biological or clinical question. In practice that has meant two complementary tracks. On the machine learning side, I have built classifiers and deep learning frameworks on oncology, neurological, hematological and endocrine datasets — ensemble models for breast cancer outcome prediction, a hybrid pipeline for Parkinson's disease diagnosis from clinical and voice features, a first-author classification study on alpha thalassemia variants, a noise-tolerant ensemble for hypothyroid classification, and PyTorch models for automated sleep apnea detection from physiological signals.

I have also contributed to a review of conventional and bioinformatics-led approaches to norovirus detection and surveillance, published in Decoding Infection and Transmission — work that sits closer to pathogen genomics than to the clinical modelling above, and that I would like to do more of.

On the genomics side, I work in Python-based bioinformatics pipelines: quality control, clustering, differential expression and cell-type annotation for single-cell RNA-seq; and differential gene expression, functional enrichment, pathway visualisation and protein–protein interaction network analysis for bulk cancer transcriptomes. My current minor research project uses the TCGA-LIHC cohort to look for prognostic biomarkers and candidate therapeutic targets in hepatocellular carcinoma.

A Summer Research Fellowship at IIEST Shibpur in 2025 sat at the join between those two tracks: designing and training PyTorch models on high-dimensional physiological signal data, with preprocessing, feature extraction and evaluation pipelines that carry over directly to large-scale sequence analysis.

I care about work being reproducible as much as accurate — end-to-end workflows, documented parameters, and results that hold up when someone else runs them. I am looking for research and applied roles where machine learning is used to answer genomics, drug-target and biomedical questions.

items.title: Integrated Bioinformatics Analysis of Hepatocellular Carcinoma
items.summary: Identifying prognostic biomarkers and candidate therapeutic targets in liver cancer from the TCGA-LIHC cohort, by chaining differential expression, functional enrichment, pathway visualisation, network analysis and drug–gene mapping into one reproducible analysis.
items.problem: Hepatocellular carcinoma is diagnosed late and has few reliable prognostic markers. Public tumour–normal transcriptome cohorts such as TCGA-LIHC hold enough signal to nominate candidate biomarkers and druggable targets, but only if expression, pathway and interaction evidence are read together rather than in isolation.
items.contribution: Designing and running the full analysis: cohort preparation, the differential expression model, the enrichment and pathway layers, construction and interrogation of the protein–protein interaction network, and the final drug–gene mapping step.

items.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analysis: Differential Expression & Cell-Type Annotation
items.summary: Reproducible, end-to-end Python workflows for scRNA-seq — quality control through clustering, differential expression and cell-type annotation — applied to public datasets to investigate disease-associated transcriptional changes and surface candidate biomarkers.
items.problem: Single-cell datasets resolve transcriptional change to individual cell types, but the analysis path from raw counts to annotated populations involves many consequential parameter choices. Without a workflow that records those choices, results are hard to reproduce or compare across datasets.
items.contribution: Engineered the workflows end to end in Python, structured so that quality-control thresholds, clustering resolution and annotation decisions are explicit and re-runnable on a new dataset.

items.title: Sleep Apnea Detection & CPAP Therapy Optimization via Deep Learning
items.summary: Deep learning frameworks in PyTorch for automated detection of sleep apnea events from physiological signals, with feature engineering and signal preprocessing, directed at informing CPAP therapy adjustment.
items.problem: Scoring apnea events from overnight physiological recordings is manual and labour-intensive, which limits how responsively CPAP therapy can be tuned. Automated detection from the signals themselves is a prerequisite for closing that loop.
items.contribution: Built the predictive frameworks: signal preprocessing, the engineered feature representation, and the PyTorch model and training setup.

outputs.label: Application of Deep Learning Techniques for Sleep Apnea Detection and CPAP Therapy Adjustment

items.title: Breast Cancer Outcome Prediction — Integrated ML Classifiers
items.summary: Ensemble machine learning classifiers applied to oncology datasets to identify prognostic features and predict survival outcomes in breast cancer.
items.problem: Prognosis in breast cancer depends on the interaction of many clinical and molecular variables. Single classifiers tend to privilege one slice of that structure; combining them gives a more stable read on which features actually carry prognostic weight.
items.contribution: Applied and compared ensemble classifiers in Scikit-learn, and carried out the prognostic feature identification and survival outcome prediction.

outputs.label: Predicting Breast Cancer Outcomes Using Integrated Machine Learning Classifiers

items.title: Parkinson's Disease Diagnosis — Hybrid ML Parameter Optimization
items.summary: A hybrid machine learning pipeline with comparative classifier analysis, designed to maximise diagnostic sensitivity on clinical and voice feature datasets.
items.problem: Voice and clinical measures carry early signal for Parkinson's disease, but which measures and which model configuration give the most sensitive diagnosis is not settled. Sensitivity matters more than raw accuracy when the cost of a missed case is high.
items.contribution: Designed the hybrid pipeline and ran the comparative classifier analysis and parameter selection with diagnostic sensitivity as the optimisation target.

outputs.label: Optimized Parameter Selection for Parkinson's Diagnosis Using a Hybrid Machine Learning Models

items.title: Alpha Thalassemia Classification via Machine Learning
items.summary: A machine learning classification model for distinguishing alpha thalassemia variants, built in Python with Scikit-learn.
items.problem: Alpha thalassemia variants differ in clinical consequence but overlap in routine hematological presentation, which makes variant-level classification from standard measurements a useful screening aid.
items.contribution: Built the classification model, including data preparation, model training and evaluation.

outputs.label: Alpha Thalassemia: A Machine Learning-Based Classification Study
